questions.q: The correct order of basic strength of the methylamines in aqueous solution is:
questions.explain: In water, inductive effect, solvation of R–NH₃⁺ and steric hindrance compete; with small methyl groups the tertiary amine loses most, giving 2° > 1° > 3° (pKb 3.27, 3.38, 4.22). The 3° > 2° > 1° order applies only in the gas phase.
In acetanilide the nitrogen lone pair is delocalised onto the carbonyl oxygen as well as the ring, so it is far less basic than aniline (conjugate-acid pKa 0.5 against 4.63).

questions.q: Which order of basicity is correct?
questions.explain: A para methyl group donates electrons and raises basicity, but almost any ortho group lowers it because the protonated –NH₃⁺ clashes with the neighbour (ortho effect).

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares pyridine and pyrrole as bases?
options: Pyrrole is more basic because its nitrogen is sp³ hybridised
Pyridine is more basic because its lone pair is in an sp² orbital outside the aromatic π system
Both are equally basic because both are aromatic nitrogen heterocycles
Pyrrole is more basic because protonation increases its aromaticity
questions.explain: Pyridine's lone pair is free to bind H⁺ (pyridinium pKa about 5.2), whereas pyrrole's lone pair is part of the aromatic sextet and protonation would destroy aromaticity.
